title: Dispatch: s02z recast_bonded_summon restores an absent familiar/steed (Sonnet 5.5, attempt 1)
description:
Implement eshyra-s02z (read it: `bd show eshyra-s02z`). Parent integration bead: eshyra-j3yp. All design decisions below are made; do not re-decide them. If something here contradicts the code or the SRD record text, stop and record the contradiction in your notes rather than improvising.

HARD RULE (bd memory srd-fidelity-hard-blocker): nothing may contradict the SRD. Source: packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1/records.json, records `spell:find-familiar` and `spell:find-steed` (`data.description`, `data.castingTime`, `data.effects[0].creation.forms`, `data.effects[0].transitions`). Do NOT edit records.json or any importer file.

## Source facts
- Find Familiar: "When the familiar drops to 0 hit points, it disappears, leaving behind no physical form. It reappears after you cast this spell again". "If you cast this spell while you already have a familiar, you instead cause it to adopt a new form. Choose one of the forms from the above list." Transition `restore-and-reform-absent-familiar` (trigger cast-again, when presence absent + link active: presence->present, operation select-new-form, reappearancePlacement creation-placement). Casting time 1 hour (ritual).
- Find Steed: "When the steed drops to 0 hit points, it disappears ... You can also dismiss your steed at any time as an action, causing it to disappear. In either case, casting this spell again summons the same steed, restored to its hit point maximum." Transition `restore-same-steed` (cast-again, absent + link active: presence->present, operation restore-same-actor, hitPoints maximum). Casting time 10 minutes. `release-bond` sets link none: no restoration after release.
- `ambiguity:find-familiar-permanent-dismissal-after-zero-hp` stays engine-pending: do not implement permanent dismissal from 0-HP absence.

## Today
Both spells are instantaneous, so they are modelled as RULING-sourced summoning effects whose actor declares `atZeroHitPoints: 'vanish-bonded'` with a durable `campaignActorId` (packages/core/src/state/activeEffects.ts ~3200-3250; toolStartEffect.ts). At 0 HP the creature becomes absent while its link and effect stay active (S50). `start_encounter` refuses to admit such an absent bonded actor (packages/core/src/state/encounterCombatants.ts ~1910-1935) because the recast was not executable.

## Decision (captain, 2026-10-04): a `recast_bonded_summon` tool
Add a model-facing tool `recast_bonded_summon` (new packages/core/src/orchestrator/toolRecastBondedSummon.ts, registered like toolRefreshEffect/toolRemoveEffectTarget in toolRegistry.ts/tools.ts; check how other tools are registered and listed in any tool-inventory tests) backed by a core operation in activeEffects.ts (export through `@eshyra/core/internal` only; root export unchanged). Args: `{ effectId, spellRef, form?: string }`.
- `spellRef` must resolve in the campaign rules stack to a spell record that has a `cast-again` transition whose `when` is `presence: absent, link: active` and changes presence->present. Derive behaviour from that transition's operation, never from the spell name:
  - `restore-same-actor` with `hitPoints: 'maximum'` (Find Steed): `form` is refused. The same campaign actor returns: status alive, hpCurrent = its effective hit point maximum (the stored hpMax adjusted by exhaustion, as everywhere else). Nothing else about the actor changes (the source names only presence and hit points; conditions, exhaustion and the 0-HP rule are left as stored).
  - `select-new-form` (Find Familiar): `form` is REQUIRED and must be a `creatureRef` listed in the record's `creation.forms` (the same form as before is allowed). The same campaign actor returns with rulesRef = that creature ref, hpMax = that creature record's hit points (use the existing readCreatureHp / lookupCreatureRecord helpers in encounterCombatants.ts), hpCurrent = hpMax, status alive. Other stored state unchanged, as above.
  - Any other operation: refuse (not executable).
- Preconditions (each a clear refusal, validated before any mutation): the effect exists, is active (not ended, not suppressed: a suppressed effect -> refuse), kind 'summoning'; it holds exactly one active actor link whose campaign actor has zero-HP rule 'vanish-bonded' and status 'absent'. Refuse when the actor is present (reform of a present or pocketed familiar is NOT in scope: say so in the refusal and file a follow-up bead), when the link was released / the effect ended (S1: with no link a cast creates a new familiar or steed: use start_effect + start_encounter), and when the actor has a combatant projection in an ACTIVE combat instance (both spells take 10 minutes or longer to cast, so the recast cannot happen mid-combat; the absent combatant row is terminal and combat closure would otherwise sync 'absent' back over the restored actor — check syncCombatantActor / closeCombatInstance and prove with a test that a restore after closure survives).
- Durable writes through an engine seam in encounterCombatants.ts (e.g. `restoreBondedCampaignActor`, mirroring removeCampaignActorFromPlay ~2720) — the only path allowed to move a campaign actor from absent back to alive, and only with the active bonded link present. Keep the mirrored `combatLifecycle` JSON consistent (status, hp, zeroHpRule stays 'vanish-bonded' so it can vanish again next time).
- Audit: append a typed effect event (new kind, e.g. 'recast', with detail { spellRef, transitionId, actor, hpCurrent, hpMax, form? }) — extend the event-kind union and detail validators and any SQL CHECK on event kinds (if the event kind column has a CHECK, that needs a migration with the next free number under packages/core/data/migrations/).
- No spell-slot spending (the model uses spend_spell_slot / ritual casting separately; say so in the tool description).
- After restoration `start_encounter` admits the actor normally (it is no longer absent). Update the start_encounter refusal text (toolStartEncounter.ts description and encounterCombatants.ts message) to point at `recast_bonded_summon` instead of "which the engine cannot yet execute", and the toolStartEffect.ts / toolUpdateCombatant.ts texts that say the return is "not yet executable".

## Docs
docs/active-effect-lifecycle.md §6 (operations list) and §8/§9 (vanish-bonded paragraphs, which currently say "not yet executable (eshyra-s02z)"): describe the executed recast, its preconditions, and what it leaves unchanged. Re-derive every sentence against the source text and the real tool contract.

## Evidence
Tests (new `packages/core/test/bondedSummonRecast.test.ts`; reuse setup helpers from zeroHpVanishAndRemovePolicy.test.ts where practical) asserting identities and exact values: steed at 0 HP -> absent -> combat closed -> recast restores the same actor id to hpMax with status alive and the link still active, then start_encounter admits it; steed under exhaustion level 4 restores to the halved effective max; familiar recast with a new form (e.g. creature:bat -> creature:owl) sets that rulesRef and that record's HP; form outside the list refused; form passed for the steed refused; recast with an active combat projection refused; recast of a present familiar refused; recast after the effect ended / link released refused; non-cast-again spell refused; restored creature can vanish again at 0 HP; the event ledger has the recast event. No count-pinned assertions.

## Procedure
Work only in this worktree. Run `npm run verify:worktree` from the worktree root BEFORE committing (it rewrites files); it must be fully green (documented skips only). Commit on this branch with a message starting `eshyra-s02z`, ending with the line `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`.
